_note: Written with AI assistance (Claude Code). Generated by scripts/build-envelope.mjs from data/reference/seed_facts.json and data/reference/link2018_table_s1.csv; never edit by hand.
estimate_note: Everything computed here is the Ignos team's order-of-magnitude reading of a NASA schematic, not a NASA measurement or model. It states no airflow for the Moon or any world: NASA reports the lunar buoyant velocity as not known (ICES-2025-392 pp. 8 and 10).

model.law: order-of-magnitude reading: g ~ (flow / flow_at_1g)^3, from flow ~ g^(1/3)
model.source: FM2 (Ferkul, LPSC 2026) PDF p. 17: a flammability-boundary schematic (T'ien 1986) whose axis is labelled 'Gravity Level (g/gEarth) or Characteristic Flow Speed (cm/s)', ticks 10-4, 10-2, 1 and 1, 4, 20. Three tick labels on a schematic, not a fit to data.

provenance.quote: The 1-g buoyant velocity was estimated by Takahashi16 to be 35 cm/s,

provenance.derived: lowest flow_cm_s among B16's Table S1 rows with a printed spread rate (Link et al. 2018 SI p. 1); a measured spread, not a quench speed
lowest flow_cm_s among B19's Table S1 rows with a printed spread rate (Link et al. 2018 SI p. 1); a measured spread, not a quench speed
lowest flow_cm_s among B12's Table S1 rows with a printed spread rate (Link et al. 2018 SI p. 1); a measured spread, not a quench speed
lowest flow_cm_s among P17's Table S1 rows with a printed spread rate (Link et al. 2018 SI p. 1); a measured spread, not a quench speed

checks.what: The g^(1/3) reading with the 20 cm/s tick against the other two ticks on the same FM2 axis
checks.result: the axis's end ticks imply an exponent of 0.325, against 1/3 in the reading

checks.what: The same reading with a square-root scaling (flow ~ g^(1/2)) instead of the cube root
checks.result: with the square root the threshold is 0.000137 to 0.0013 g and the Moon sits 127 to 1200 times above it; with the cube root, 3540 to 103000. Under either, at least about 100 times above, so only that floor is robust to the exponent

checks.what: The two 1 g anchors disagree, so the band carries both
checks.result: 35 cm/s is 1.75 times 20 cm/s; every threshold here is a band between them

checks.what: Normal gravity: the flame makes its own flow, so cutting a slow forced flow does not stop it
checks.result: consistent: Link et al. 2018 (Sci. Rep. 8:120, p. 5) report spread nearly independent of forced flow below the buoyant flow, and no low-flow extinction in normal gravity

checks.what: Orbit: with no gravity-driven flow, a slow enough forced flow lets the flame die
checks.result: consistent: Link et al. 2018 (p. 4-5) report no flame spread below 0.6 cm/s for B16 and B19; Table S1 shows B12 and P17 still spreading at 0.48 and 0.41 cm/s, so these flows are lowest measured spreads, not quench speeds, and the threshold is an 'at most'

caveats: An order-of-magnitude reading of three tick labels on a NASA schematic (FM2 PDF p. 17, T'ien 1986), not a model fitted to data and not a measurement. It gives gravity levels only, never an airflow for the Moon: NASA reports the lunar buoyant velocity as not known (ICES-2025-392 pp. 8 and 10).

The cube root is read from a schematic, not fitted. With a square-root scaling the Moon sits 127 to 1200 times above the threshold instead of 3540 to 103000; only "at least about 100 times above, under either scaling" is robust (checks: exponent-sensitivity).

Table S1's sub-1 cm/s flow labels (0.41 to 0.83 cm/s), which set this threshold, are the least certain numbers in the data: NASA's on-screen air sensor (whole cm/s) reads 0 in most low-flow steps and 2 at the 0.82 cm/s steps, so it cannot confirm them, and NASA's fan calibrations do not reproduce them (team check, docs/research/accuracy/air_display/README.md). Treat them as approximate.
Table S1's lowest flows are where spread was still measured, in tests at different oxygen and rod sizes, not quench speeds; so the threshold gravity is 'at most' that value.
The 1 g flow comes from a NASA slide (20 cm/s) and an Earth estimate (35 cm/s, Takahashi); they differ by a factor of 1.75, and the band carries both.
Gravity only: oxygen also matters (more oxygen lets a flame live on less flow), and that axis is not in this file.
Rod samples of black PMMA only (Link et al. 2018); other materials and shapes may differ.
